approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill raises customs processing fees for freight shipments worth $10,000 or more starting 1 January 2014.
It creates two fee levels and expands the range of costs recovered by the Australian Customs and Border Protection Service to include community protection expenses.
The charge for sea consignments filed electronically rises from $50.00 to $152.60 and for manual lodgment from $65.75 to $152.60.
Increase import processing charges on air, sea and post consignments valued at $10,000 or more.
Introduce a two-tiered charging structure to keep increases small relative to the value of higher-valued goods.
Broaden the cost base of import processing charges to recover all of the ACBPS's cargo and trade related costs, including community protection costs.
Importers of commercial freight shipments arriving by air, sea or post whose customs value reaches $10,000 or more.

Moved that the bill be read a second time, stating that from 1 January 2014 it will increase import processing charges for air, sea and post consignments valued at $10,000 or more, broaden cost recovery for border activities, and generate an estimated additional $674.3 million across the forward estimates.

Summed up debate on the Import Processing Charges Amendment Bill, a revenue measure inherited from Labor's own 2013-14 budget that will raise an estimated $674.3 million over the forward estimates from consignments worth $10,000 or more, and said the previous government had cut more than $750 million from Customs and Border Protection, reducing staff from 5,700 to a projected 4,400.
